articles.title: AirPods Pro 3 review: tripling down on a good thing
articles.summary: The $250 AirPods Pro 3 deliver excellent active noise cancellation, improved sound and fit, hands-free fitness tracking, and live AI-powered translations.
articles.body: The AirPods Pro are about as ubiquitous as earbuds can get. Step outside your door, and you’re almost certain to see people wearing them. For good reason, too. Their active noise cancelling (ANC) is excellent for the price, sound quality is great, and they’re comfortable and convenient. If it ain’t broke, why fix it? After all, messing with a winning formula just for the sake of change often ends up in disappointment. That’s not the case with the $249.99 AirPods Pro 3. Of all the shiny new gadgets Apple launched last week, this is the sole no-brainer upgrade. Everything you liked about the AirPods Pro just got better — and so did everything you didn’t. [Product: AirPods Pro 3 | Better fit The second-gen Pro was more or less about refining the software and sound; the overall design didn’t change. But while the AirPods Pro 3 look familiar at a glance, pop them in your ear and you’ll feel the difference. The new buds and tips are more angled, so they slot more naturally into your ear canal. You can twist them in for a more secure fit, whereas the last AirPods Pro would pop out unless you put them in just right. Another plus: Apple now includes five ear tip sizes, adding an XXS size so you have a better chance of finding a comfy fit. That said, I would temper any expectations regarding the “foam-infused” tips. These aren’t your traditional foam tips, which expand to fit your ear more securely. What Apple’s done here is more of a hybrid approach. The front portion has some foam that subtly expands, but the majority of the tip is silicone for comfort and easier cleaning. [Image: [Image: [Image: Fit has always been one of the biggest complaints with AirPods, regardless of model. Whenever I come across AirPods haters, the usual reasons are either that the buds are too uncomfortable or they simply slip out. My spouse has bought multiple pairs over the years because the buds are always falling out of their ears. Nary a day goes by that I don’t find them crouching next to the bed or sofa, phone flashlight out, searching underneath for a missing AirPod. With these, they immediately declared, “They fit so much better!” and proceeded to pre-order their own pair. I’ve heard similar reactions from fellow reviewers who also had issues with the fit on prior AirPods Pro. Still, that’s not a huge sample size, and everyone’s ear shape is unique. While I think the Pro 3 will fit more people, I still recommend trying a pair before committing if you’ve had issues in the past. But as someone who hasn’t, these fit me better too. World’s best ANC? At Apple’s keynote last week, Apple executives kept saying these things had the “world’s best ANC” for wireless in-ear headphones. The claim is that the active noise cancellation in the third-gen buds is twice as good as the second gen, and four times better than the originals. The sound quality is also purportedly better due to a redesigned internal architecture that Apple says improves airflow for better bass. Now, I’m not an audio engineer, but I did put the AirPods Pro 3’s ANC through a series of real-life tests alongside my personal pair of AirPods Pro 2. It’s pretty damn good. The first test was a six-and-a-half hour flight from San Francisco to New York. Both pairs of buds performed well, but the third-gen were noticeably better. The dull hum of the plane was completely eliminated, though I could still hear announcements if I didn’t have audio playing. (That’s typical for any ANC headphones, however, especially earbuds.) [Image: The case for the AirPods Pro 3 also has stronger Find My capabilities this year. My second test was sitting in my kitchen while my spouse and in-laws were fixing our broken garbage disposal and running the laundry. Again, the second and third-gen buds were comparable, but the latter were notably better at dampening higher frequencies like voices and my cats yowling for kibble. If I put my tunes on, I couldn’t hear anything. I also tested the active noise cancellation at a Bob Dylan and Willie Nelson concert against the Loop Experience 2 and EarPeace Music passive earplugs, which reduce noise by 17db and 20db respectively. The third-gen buds outperformed the Loop Experience 2, and were roughly on par with the Earpeace Music. I normally wouldn’t use AirPods in lieu of earplugs at a concert, but it’s nice to know that they’ll do in a pinch. As for sound quality, the improvement is subtle but definitely there. I noticed it most while listening to the K-Pop Demon Hunters soundtrack. Multi-part vocal harmonies in songs like “Golden,” “Your Idol,” and “What It Sounds Like” are more audible, while the bass lines are punchier. Despite listening to this album on repeat since June with the AirPods Pro 2, I noticed new elements in the sound production, like faint bubble-popping effects in the catchy “Soda Pop.” I had a similar experience listening to old favorites. And while I still think spatial audio is gimmicky outside of a Vision Pro, I can appreciate that sound quality has been subtly improved on Dolby Atmos tracks as well. Ultimately, you’ll notice a richer overall listening experience regardless of whether you’re listening to music or watching an immersive movie. --- Specs Sensors: Dual beamforming microphones, inward-facing microphone, skin-detecting sensor, motion-detecting accelerometer, speech-detecting accelerometer, heart rate sensor, touch control. Chips: H2 headphone chip, U2 chip in charging case Dust and water resistance: IP57 Battery: Estimated 8 hours of listening time with ANC, 7.5 hours with Spatial Audio and Head tracking enabled. 6.5 hours with heart rate sensing during workouts. 10 hours in Transparency mode. 24 hours with the case. Connectivity: Bluetooth 5.3 --- Calls sound “generically good,” according to a friend I called while walking along a windy highway full of bustling cars. They weren’t able to hear any of the wind or environmental noise, even though the ANC wasn’t able to wipe them out entirely for me. ANC is power-intensive, but I was pleased to see the third-gen buds have improved battery life. I wore them with ANC enabled for five hours of my flight, plus a 10-minute wait at baggage claim and a 40-minute Uber ride home. I still had 27 percent battery left by the time I got home. Altogether, my usage roughly tracks with Apple’s eight-hour estimate for ANC listening time on a single charge. Hands-free fitness tracking Perhaps the biggest hardware update for the AirPods Pro 3 is the addition of a heart rate sensor, enabling fitness tracking without an Apple Watch. It’s not a huge surprise, given that Apple added heart rate sensors to the Powerbeats Pro 2 earlier this year. But the AirPods Pro do a lot more with the feature. For starters, you can track your heart rate during 50 types of workouts directly from the native iOS Fitness app. On the Powerbeats, this was limited to a handful of partner apps at launch. This is great news for folks with wrist tattoos, which get in the way of smartwatch sensors, or those who’d rather not wear smart rings, chest straps, or smartwatches for sports like boxing or weight lifting. It’s also a boon for anyone who routinely forgets their Apple Watch while on walks. [Image: You can choose to track workouts with the Apple Watch or with just the AirPods Pro 3. Apple’s Fitness Plus app can display heart rate data from the AirPods Pro 3 — a strange omission from the Powerbeats at launch. Crucially, the AirPods can also act as a secondary heart rate data stream when used with the Apple Watch. Previously, apps always deferred to the Apple Watch over the Powerbeats. Now, Apple’s introduced an algorithm that will analyze which of the two heart rate data streams has a stronger signal in a given activity, and prefer that one. Some good news: Apple isn’t gatekeeping these improvements to the AirPods. It’s since announced these updates will also come to the Powerbeats in iOS 26. I tried Pro 3-only tracking for two outdoor walks and found that the heart rate tracking was comparable to a chest strap, within roughly 5 to 10 beats per minute. Accuracy will heavily depend on a secure fit, but I never had issues getting readings, even when I got sweaty. Some more good news on that front: the buds now have IP57 sweat and water resistance. I wouldn’t dunk my head in a pool while wearing them, but they might stand a better chance of surviving the wash or a sudden downpour. Semi-lost in translation As part of Apple Intelligence, the AirPods Pro 3 (along with the Pro 2 and AirPods 4) will support live translations for a handful of languages. I’ve always wanted the Babel fish from Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy to be real, so I was stoked to try this out. Compared to phones or smartwatches, earbuds feel like a more natural choice for live translation tech. Sorry to burst any bubbles. This live translation feature is no Babel fish, though I can see it being useful in a handful of scenarios. The feature was impressive in a live demo Apple gave me where a Spanish speaker gave a short speech. I activated Live Translation via the iPhone’s Action Button and voilá. (You can also activate by pinching both AirPods’ stems). The speaker’s voice was dampened and after a short, intentional delay, Apple Intelligence crisply translated what was being said on-device. You and your conversation partner can either both use AirPods for translation, or if they don’t have a pair, you can also view a transcript of the translated conversation on your iPhone. And if it worked like this every single time, I’d cry tears of joy. [Image: [Image: [Image: But real-life conversations are a bit different. They’re not always calm. They’re full of ums and uhs, and I doubt there’s any child of immigrants who hasn’t heard an auntie rattle off at the speed of light. So I called up my cousin’s spouse, who is a fluent German speaker, to see how this feature would handle translation without guardrails. To both of our surprise, it actually worked quite well for conversational German. It was even able to accurately translate when he spoke in German slang in an Austrian accent — something he said might be hard for a native German speaker. (He likened it to hearing someone with a thick Scottish accent.) It only stumbled when he would occasionally switch back to English to comment on accuracy. The feature isn’t limited to in-person conversations only, however. It works with any audio you’re hearing in person, meaning you should be able to use it for public announcements while traveling, video calls, or foreign-language media. To test this, I watched a scene from the German film Der Untergang featuring an epic meltdown from Hitler in the last days of his dictatorship. I chose this scene precisely because the actor speaks quickly and with emotion, changing thoughts mid-sentence, and there’s cross-talk from other characters. (And because I could compare the translation with the official subtitles.) [Image: [Image: [Image: The translation feature performed admirably, but struggled to recognize character names or account for abrupt pauses in dialogue. Sometimes it identified the words correctly but used the wrong meaning for the context. For example, a line that Live Translation presented as “Steiner could not massage enough forces for an attack” is translated in the movie’s subtitles as “Steiner didn’t have enough force to attack.” A more literal translation would be “Steiner couldn’t amass enough forces for the attack.” There are multiple ways you can translate the word that became “massage,” but Live Translation picked the wrong one. This isn’t an Apple limitation; I’ve seen it across all AI translation tech. But while live translation works well enough to convey broad meaning, it’s hard to say whether people will use this as intended. I’ve lived abroad and have a multilingual family. To me, using AirPods makes most sense in trying to translate announcements, museum tours where multilingual options aren’t available, or media that may not yet have subtitles. In face-to-face human interaction, most people are happy to gesture or point to a translation app on their phones. And in business meetings where the absolute correct meaning is crucial, it’s hard to beat seasoned interpreters. I’ll be curious to try this out during an upcoming trip to Italy, but I have the sense that doing so will also come with a healthy dose of anxiety and self-consciousness. [Image: Now that I’ve used the AirPods Pro 3, I can’t go back. A no-brainer upgrade Let me preface this by saying you shouldn’t run out and buy these if your AirPods Pro 2 are working perfectly fine. There’s no reason to throw out a good pair of earbuds. Ideally, I’d ask that everyone exercise restraint and only upgrade when their current AirPods finally crap out or are genuinely in need of replacement. (If you’re coming from the original AirPods Pro, you’ve got a much better case for upgrading.) But I also know how gadget nerd brains work. If you’re going to ignore me, yes this is a worthy upgrade. I wrote ahead of last week’s event that Apple should lean into giving people what they want, and they’ve done that with the AirPods Pro 3. I have next to no complaints, and the only downside I can think of is perhaps the improved fit still won’t work for everyone. The price is the same, the new additions are smart, and most importantly, the sound quality and ANC are top-notch for earbuds. I’m happy with my AirPods Pro 2, but I won’t lie. Now that I’ve experienced the AirPods Pro 3, I can’t go back. I’ll be ordering a pair for myself once I return this review unit. --- Agree to continue: AirPods Pro 3 Every smart device now requires you to agree to a series of terms and conditions before you can use it — contracts that no one actually reads. It’s impossible for us to read and analyze every single one of these agreements. But we’re going to start counting exactly how many times you have to hit “agree” to use devices when we review them since these are agreements most people don’t read and definitely can’t negotiate. Like any other Bluetooth earbuds, the AirPods Pro can technically be set up and used without you agreeing to anything in software. With the new heart rate tracking feature, however, you may optionally be asked to agree to third-party privacy policies and terms of service if you agree to share that data (i.e., Ladder, Runna, etc.) * Apple’s warranty agreement Final tally is one mandatory agreement.

articles.title: Best Free Weapons to Find Early - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: When you're just starting out in GTA 6, you may find yourself wanting more firearm options available to you. While you can't permanently acquire
articles.body:
When you're just starting out in GTA 6 , you may find yourself wanting more firearm options available to you. While you can't permanently acquire regular enemy weapons, there are Unique Weapon Variants that you can unlock by simply finding them, and a number of them can be found with minimal resistance. Here are some the best weapons you can find for free in Grand Theft Auto VI, even at the start of the game.

Note that these Unique Weapon Variants are locked versions of particular weapons. The mods that they come equipped with are locked with these variants, so if you want a version of these weapons that you can modify as you see fit, you'll have to save up and purchase the stock version from Ammu-nation.

Small spoiler warning! - Most of these weapons are associated with small stories that involve random characters throughout Leonida. We'll avoid the specifics of these story moments in this guide page so you can discover them for yourself.

Down the road from Jason's safehouse in Key Lento is a building hiding a surprise weapon. In the south of Key Lento, near the police station, is the Leonida Key Lento Mini Mart. North-west of the mini mart, directly across the road behind the shop is a stilt house with a couch on the lawn. The house to the left has a manatee mailbox, close to the couch.

You need to break in to the house on the upper level, and then walk to the bedroom in the southern end of the house. There's an ensuite bathroom here, and just behind the door is a shotgun, the Unpacked Comshot 12 .

This weapon's main selling points are that it's a more modern pump-action shotgun that you can unlock early. It has a magazine size of 7, so you can take out a whole group of enemies with this weapon very quickly. The sight isn't too useful when you consider that it's a shotgun (unless you really like aiming in first person with Right Stick Click / Right Stick Click ), but it fires much faster than the basic pump action shotguns that you can buy in Key Lento.

The Cruel Huntsman's SM-69 Sniper Rifle is easy to find if you go to the right place out in Gullet Marsh in Mariana County . North of the Sunrise RV Park Kingfisher Illegal Operation is a small shack. It's the only building nearby, so it's easy to see on the map.

When you arrive, you can find a hunting shack, and there's a body that's stuck halfway through the window. Underneath the body on the outside of the shack is the Cruel Huntsman's SM-69 Sniper Rifle .

This sniper is great to get early, as it gives you a long-range rifle for hunting or for attacking an enemy base from a distance. The rifle comes equipped with a scope that you can use by pressing Right Stick Click / Right Stick Click while aiming down sights. This scope is set to a fixed level of magnification.

The damage the rifle dishes out is more than the damage of the early sniper rifle that you can buy, and it's infinitely cheaper to acquire!

Inside the same shack where you found the Cruel Huntsman's Sniper is a revolver that you can also pick up for free, the Swamp Bait Akulus Revolver .

This revolver is a 6-shot heavy revolver. It deals decent damage, one-shotting enemies up-close and two-shotting enemies at mid-range. It doesn't have terrific accuracy, so it's best to use this weapon from behind cover while stationary, or at close-medium range so that you don't miss too many shots.

Paired with a standard pistol, the revolver makes a great secondary firearm that packs a punch.

North-west of Southwind , past the Mile Zero Air Station , is a cluster of small islands. To the north of those islands, if you're swimming or using a boat in that area, you may come across a bunch of packages and debris floating in the water.

If you dive into the water where the debris is located, you should see a sunken speedboat on the ocean floor.

Grab the nearby illicit product, and then look under the side of the sunken boat to find the Drug Mule KZ-59 Assault Rifle . It may be a little rusty, and you might want to replace it when you get some cash, but a rifle like this one can fire a lot of bullets in a short span of time, so if you're looking to take on a tough Illegal Operation or get into some trouble with the cops, make sure to bring along a rifle like this one.

Conspiracist Type 9 Machine Pistol (and Launcher)

Exploring a little further afield, to the north-west of Vice City in Balsero (next to the Griffin Shooting Range , south of the Black Eagle Ammu-Nation shop) is a trailer. Head inside the trailer through the door on one of the sides and look for a bunker hatch. Down the hatch is a bunch of healing consumables, grenades, and also the Conspiracist Type 9 Machine Pistol . This is an automatic sidearm that that you can fire while driving a vehicle, which is perfect for trying to pop tires while you're making a getaway. It also comes equipped with many modifications that help to increase the range, accuracy and magazine size of the weapon.

There's another weapon in this bunker that you can pick up, known as the Hauners H-AT Launcher . This is an unowned weapon , so you can't keep this one forever when you pick it up, but you can still use it until you get wasted or leave it behind for one reason or another. The Hauners H-AT Launcher is a great little rocket launcher. It comes with five rounds when you pick it up, and you can definitely get into some trouble with the police with this thing.

South-east of Port Gellhorn is Leonida State Prison . Not far to the north of the prison is a house and a barn alongside it.

Enter the barn by breaking down the door, and inside is an open hatch that you can descend into. At the bottom is a tunnel, and all the way at the end of it is the Convict Kalinga .50 Cal Pistol .

It comes equipped with a tactical light (which you can toggle while aiming down sights by pressing D-pad Up on the D-pad), and also a scope (which you can activate while aiming down sights with Right Stick Click / Right Stick Click ) which is perfect for this weapon because it is so powerful that you can use it a medium-long ranges. The stopping power of this weapon is so devastating that it can one-shot most unarmored enemies.

Pair that with the fact this is a sidearm and you will practically never be outgunned while you have this pistol equipped.

If you're interested in finding more destructive equipment early in your GTA 6 playthrough, you can find IGN's official Grand Theft Auto VI guide pages for how to get a Rhino tank, as well as how to get and use Sticky Bombs.

Up Next: How to Get a Rocket Launcher in Chapter 1

articles.title: LEGO Black Friday Deals Are Here
articles.body:
We made it, friends. Black Friday has arrived, which means all the sales are now live across the entire retail landscape. Anyone interested in saving money on LEGO has a nice variety of deals available, on everything from recently released sets, all the way to sets scheduled to retire soon. These are the best LEGO deals for Black Friday 2026.

If you want to look at all of the Black Friday LEGO deals, you can go straight to the source at the retailers above. You'll find dozens upon dozens of sets on sale for up to 50% off, which is about the lowest you can ever expect to see LEGO sets drop, even during clearance sales. For categorized groups of LEGO Black Friday deals, read on.

Each year on Black Friday LEGO releases a major new set. This year's Black Friday set is LEGO Godzilla , an imposing set that stands over two feet tall and features the King of Monsters shooting a heat ray toward the sky. We built this set and found it to be even more impressive in person.

LEGO Star Wars Imperial Lambda-Class Shuttle

LEGO Star Wars The Mandalorian's N-1 Starfighter

LEGO Star Wars The Mandalorian: Grogu with Hover Pram

LEGO Star Wars: The Phantom Menace Battle Droid with STAP

LEGO Star Wars TIE Fighter with Imperial Hangar Rack

LEGO Star Wars: Ahsoka Chopper (C1-10P) Astromech Droid

LEGO Star Wars Imperial Remnant AT-RT Driver Helmet

There hasn't been a shortage of LEGO Star Wars sets for roughly a quarter century. I think they keep getting better and better as older sets retire and new sets replace them. Of the many sets on sale, I built the Phantom Menace Battle Drone set, which is quite a bit bigger than I had expected – something that doesn't happen often when it comes to LEGO. I recommend it.

LEGO Animal Crossing Isabelle’s House Visit

LEGO Pokémon Iconic Trainer Moments Poké Ball

LEGO and video games go together like peanut butter and chocolate. From Fortnite to Mario to Pokémon , you can find tons of video game-based LEGO sets on sale for Black Friday.

Mattel Brick Shop Xbox Console Building Set

While it's not an actual LEGO set, it's certainly LEGO-adjacent. Mattel Brick Shop is a pretty recent LEGO competitor that makes sets based on things LEGO doesn't do. Like this original Xbox, for instance, which comes complete with a buildable Duke controller and a handful of little dioramas hidden inside, just like the LEGO PlayStation I built a couple months ago.

LEGO Disney and Pixar Toy Story Alien with Pizza Planet Rocket Ride

LEGO Disney Frozen Olaf and Bruni’s Picnic Fun

LEGO and Disney is another great combination, because both companies make things that appeal to both kids and adults alike. A good number of LEGO Disney and Pixar sets are on sale for Black Friday, including some great options if you don't want to break the bank.

BrickHeadz Eleven, Max, Demogorgon and Holly Figures

Star Wars: The Phantom Menace Battle Droid with STAP

Unlike most retailers, the LEGO Store actually waited until Black Friday to kick off its Black Friday sale ( see it here ). It features discounts on a lot of sets that aren't on sale everywhere else, like the adorable Wicket the Ewok and the BrickHeadz Eeyore. In fact, most of these sets are retiring soon, which means this might be the last time you can grab them for a discount. And if that's not enough, LEGO Insiders ( sign up here for free ) can get 4x loyalty points on a whole bunch of sets as well.

LEGO ONE PIECE The Going Merry Pirate Ship

LEGO ONE PIECE Buggy the Clown’s Circus Tent

The LEGO One Piece partnership is actually based on the live-action Netflix series rather than the anime. But that series hews so close to the original material that it doesn't really matter once the sets are translated into brick-built form.

LEGO Harry Potter Diagon Alley Wizarding Shops

LEGO Harry Potter Privet Drive: Aunt Marge’s Visit

LEGO Harry Potter Book Nook: Hogwarts Express

LEGO Harry Potter Forbidden Forest: Expecto Patronum

There's no shortage of LEGO Harry Potter sets , especially with the upcoming new HBO adaptation of the series about to kick off on Christmas day, which is getting its own line of LEGO sets starting in January. A decent number of movie-based sets are on sale now for Black Friday.

LEGO Shrek: Shrek, Donkey & Puss in Boots

LEGO Jurassic World Dinosaur Fossils Triceratops Skull

LEGO Technic Lamborghini Huracán Tecnica Orange

LEGO Technic PEUGEOT 9X8 24H Le Mans Hybrid Hypercar

LEGO Creator 3-in-1 Forest Animals: Red Fox

LEGO Editions FIFA World Cup Official Trophy

LEGO Creator 3-in-1 Space Exploration Telescope

LEGO Technic Mack LR Electric Garbage Truck

An excellent assortment of other sets are also on sale, many of which have proved very popular with IGN readers. We built the brand-new LEGO Shrek set and loved it. Many of the discounted sets are aimed at adults and intended for display, rather than play.

If you're looking for a fun way to spruce up your abode for Christmas, LEGO sets are a great way to do it. First, you get the fun of building the set. Then you can use it as a colorful decoration around the house. That's a win-win, especially when the sets in question are on sale for Black Friday.

LEGO Star Wars SMART Play: Mos Eisley Cantina

LEGO Star Wars SMART Play: Yoda’s Hut and Jedi Training

LEGO Star Wars SMART Play: Luke’s Landspeeder

LEGO Star Wars SMART Play: AT-ST Attack on Endor

LEGO Pokémon SMART Play: Mewtwo’s Lab Break

LEGO Pokémon SMART Play: Drone Search for Mythical Mew

A number of Smart Play LEGO sets are also on sale. These are in the LEGO Star Wars and LEGO Pokémon themes. However, none of the Smart Play sets on sale right now actually include a Smart Brick, which happens to be the key to the whole Smart Play thing. On their own, these sets won’t light up or make sounds. You need a set that comes with a Smart Brick to take full advantage of those sets.

LEGO Technic Fast and Furious Toyota Supra MK4

LEGO Harry Potter Knockturn Alley Wizarding Shops

Macy's, the department store known for its big annual Thanksgiving day parade, also sells LEGO sets. Who knew? Most of the deals are either not terribly remarkable, with modest 20% discounts, but a handful of sets have 50% discounts. Take a look using the links above.

If you want to buy some LEGO sets for yourself or anyone on your gift list this year, now is the time to do so. You won't find lower prices before Christmas, and probably not for a good while into 2027. I expect most of the above deals that don't sell out will be available through Cyber Monday. But seriously, it's smarter to buy sooner than later, because the best deals will sell out.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

Cheat codes in Grand Theft Auto VI work differently than in previous GTA games in that they are unlocked only after beating the final mission. Once you've done so, you unlock a Cheats menu that reveals cheat codes that you must unlock individually by completing Cheat Challenges – only then will you be able to view the cheat codes and input them. This official guide contains a list of GTA 6 cheats and cheat codes on PlayStation 5 and Xbox, cheat button input commands, and how to unlock cheats.

TLDR : You cannot use cheats until the end of the game and even then, you must unlock them before you can use them.

Click on a link below to jump to that section of this guide:

Here’s a quick list of the best cheats and which cheats to unlock first in GTA 6 (Editor’s Note: these are the ones we Iike the most and I think you will, too. – Samuel Claiborn, GTA 6 IGN Guide Editor) :

D-pad Up D-pad Right D-pad Down D-pad Left D-pad Up D-pad Left D-pad Down D-pad Right – Instantly gives you $250,000.

D-pad Down D-pad Up D-pad Right D-pad Down D-pad Left D-pad Left D-pad Up D-pad Down D-pad Down D-pad Down – Infinite ammo, no reloading needed.

D-pad Down D-pad Up D-pad Up D-pad Down D-pad Up D-pad Down D-pad Up D-pad Down D-pad Up D-pad Right – Infinite Focus.

D-pad Down D-pad Up D-pad Left D-pad Up D-pad Up D-pad Up D-pad Up D-pad Up D-pad Down D-pad Down – Adds body armor to your loadout.

Note that there is no Infinite Life code or Invincibility code in GTA 6, though some mitigate damage in the full list below and the Body Armor cheat helps. There is also no Lower Wanted Level cheat this time around, so beware of shenanigans!

You must unlock every cheat code in GTA 6 before you can use them. But before you can start doing this, you must beat the final mission of Grand Theft Auto VI, roll credits, and return to the post-game (don’t forget to start a manual save here!). The post-game takes you right before the final mission to the “point of no return” so you can explore before the consequences of GTA 6’s ending events.

After entering the post-game, a Cheats menu appears on the Progress menu screen at the far right (Pro tip: You can actually press D-pad Left once to reach this menu to jump to the far Cheats menu).

Now, each cheat code has to be unlocked by completing a Cheat Challenge, and the Cheat Challenges are listed in this menu and in our tables below. But here’s some good news: you probably have unlocked a few cheat codes already by simply playing GTA 6 to the ending!

When you complete a Cheat Challenge, a message will pop up informing you that the cheat is unlocked. You can now enter the cheat code freely any time to activate it.

Here are some commonly asked questions and answers about GTA 6’s cheat codes.

Q: Can I enter cheats before unlocking them?

A: No, you cannot – even if you read the cheats above and enter them, they will not work until you have beat GTA 6’s final mission and unlocked the cheat by completing the associated Cheat Challenge.

Q: Can I use cheat codes to make Main Missions easier?

A: No, because all cheat codes unlock only after completing the game. However, if you go to the Pause Menu, select Settings > Gameplay > Accessibility, you can toggle on a few things to make Main Missions and gameplay easier. For instance, you can toggle on Reduced Vehicle Damage, Accessible Combat, and Simplified Mini Games, among other things that won't affect your Achievements and Trophies but will make GTA 6 easier.

Q: Do cheats disable trophies and achievements?

A: Yes. You cannot earn trophies or achievements while a cheat code is active.

Q: Why can't I save my game after using a cheat code?

A: Cheats are just for fun in the post-game and are not intended to aid with progression, therefore both manual and auto saving are disabled after activating a cheat code.

Q: Is there an invincibility cheat code?

A: No, there is no cheat to give infinite health. There is a cheat code to nullify fall damage, though, and one to repair your current vehicle.

Q: Are there cheat phone numbers in GTA 6?

A: No, you can only enter cheat codes by opening the phone with D-pad Up , then holding L1 + R1 / LB + RB and inputting the code.

Q: Which GTAVI cheat codes are the hardest to unlock?

A: Migraine, a cheat that applies a distorted filter, requires you to survive 6 minutes with a 6-star wanted level, which is pretty brutal. Additionally, spawning a Hauners P-996 LAZER aircraft will be difficult as you need to complete every single in-game challenge to unlock it.

articles.title: Despite Take-Two Takedown, Vibecoding Teen Behind Nuked GTA 6 PC Port Project 'Leonida' Vows to Continue
articles.summary: The 15-year-old vibecoder behind a GTA 6 PC port project Take-Two recently shut down has vowed to continue their work despite the potential for further action from the company.
articles.body:
The 15-year-old vibecoder behind a GTA 6 PC port project Take-Two recently shut down has vowed to continue their work despite the potential for further action from the company.

‘NotRexed’ is behind ‘Project Leonida,’ which was at one point leading the race to create a PC port of GTA 6 following the recent leak of an Xbox build. Cyberleek, the infamous leaker behind many early GTA 6 gameplay clips, reportedly released the Xbox build of GTA 6 last week, and vibecoders have been attempting to port the game to PC since.

Fueled by AI, progress has been swift, with clips showing GTA 6 running on PC at a higher frame rate than on console, and one video even showing basic multiplayer. Obviously, Rockstar Games, which will no doubt release GTA 6 on PC officially at some point, and parent company Take-Two will be watching the homebrew scene’s every move like a hawk.

In the case of Project Leonida, Take-Two has already taken action. NotRexed was organizing and sharing work on a Discord group, and hosting their findings on a GitHub repository, when cease and desists from Take-Two hauled everything offline. NotRexed then took to social media to announce they'd decided to call it a day.

“I quit guys. I’m sorry,” NotRexed said. “I really want to make cool stuff but every single time s**t happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the Discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.”

NotRexed went on to insist that they were finding it tough to run Project Leonida while also going to school. “Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15-year-old kid,” they said. “Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.”

However, NotRexed has now returned, and promised to continue the project. “Ignore my other posts,” NotRexed said after changing their mind. “Something’s coming soon. Leonida is NOT dead. I have been doing a lot of work behind the scenes. I’ll have some stuff to show all of you soon.”

IGN spoke to NotRexed to find out why they’re doing this, whether they understand the risks, what they’ll do if they get in legal trouble, and what their parents think of it all.

“It’s just a hobby of mine,” NotRexed said in a private message. “I started doing similar things with porting games to the web back in the start of 2026, and I’ve always just thought of it to be cool.”

Before generative AI, NotRexed had no interest in porting games to other platforms, they said. But after finding out it was possible in 2025, they’re now taking on one of the most powerful publishers in video games. Interestingly, there’s no real motive behind it.

“I’ve always been interested in tech and mess around with it a lot,” they said. According to them, even their parents are aware of what they do and are largely supportive of it. “Yes, they know about all my projects and work I do, and they’re pretty encouraging about it,” they claimed.

It made me wonder if they were fully aware of the legal risks involved in such an undertaking. “Yea, they have warned me about what could happen,” NotRexed insisted when I asked if their parents knew about the potential legal issues. “I’m still continuing my work as of now tho because even tho T2 took down my repo and Discord they have never sent an email or message directly to me. If I do get into legal trouble I’m probably gonna stop working on it but possibly have a friend continue it.”

How feasible is this? IGN asked Matt Freedman, a veteran game developer with expertise in both traditional development and the controversial emerging technology of AI.

“A recompilation is different from a port,” Freedman said. “But yes, an AI driven recompilation of GTA 6 is very doable and wouldn't have the same 'game feel' problems that an AI-driven port would have.”

He went on to explain the differences between decompilations, recompilations, and ports. A decomp is where someone manually reverse engineers a game to run on other systems, like the Mario 64 PC port. “This is very time consuming and requires a human to do the work and effectively 'guess' how the game works,” he said.

A port takes existing assets or creates new ones and essentially builds a new version of the same game to work on another system. The Witcher 3’s Switch port is an example of this. “A team took The Witcher 3 code base and assets and then modified them by hand to work on the Switch,” he said.

For recomps, people use large language models (LLMs) to break down a game and rebuild it, essentially reverse engineering the title for whatever system the user wants. “Since LLMs natively can read binary, they're able to understand the specific code better than humans can,” Freedman explained.

A decomp or port of GTA 6 would not be easy — not least because Rockstar uses proprietary tech, including its in-house Rage engine, to power its games. “When it comes to AI, it'll depend on how well it has previously seen the engine or the low level SDK,” Freedman replied when asked about this complication. “A well studied proprietary engine with lots of public information would be easier for it to understand. A custom engine for an obscure CPU would be much more difficult for it.

“So, something like Rockstar's Rage engine would be more difficult for it to figure out than something like a game made in Unreal. But… given that a 15-year-old was able to have an AI port GTA 6 to PC, it's clearly not the biggest lift out there.”

All the while, Take-Two is working to take down various homebrew community efforts from GitHub, as the race to release an unofficial GTA 6 PC port appears close to the finish line. There’s even a website tracking the various attempts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC.

The big question for Take-Two is, can it do anything meaningful to stop a working, playable build of GTA 6 on PC from getting into people's hands? GitHub takedowns can only go so far, as the homebrew scene uses AI to speed along development. It's a question IGN recently asked when people started to work on a PC port of Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake .

Take-Two stands to make billions of dollars more from the official PC release of GTA 6, so any unofficial version is a significant business risk. In a recent interview with IGN sister site RPS , former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible , due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports.

Earlier this month, Strauss Zelnick, the boss of Take-Two, responded to the threat of AI-assisted reverse-engineering and decompilation of games in an interview with IGN. He said he was taking the issue seriously, and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version.

IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it?

Strauss Zelnick: I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business. I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.

IGN: Related, last week Anthropic confirmed they took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games. I would assume you would welcome that. And would you like to see other AI companies like OpenAI do the same thing to prevent people from using these powerful AI models to clone your games?

Strauss Zelnick: I think all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's. And if you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected.

During an investor-focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, attended by IGN, Zelnick was asked multiple times about the AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up.

“This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations.

“That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.”

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: Former Gran Turismo World Series Competitor Helped Tune GTA 6 Car Physics
articles.summary: A former Gran Turismo World Series competitor helped Rockstar tune GTA 6's car physics.
articles.body:
A lot of people have complained about the Ganado, Jason’s starting car in GTA 6 , for being tricky to drive. The small pickup is a little unwieldy and prone to swinging out at the back end because it’s based on the Ford Ranchero, a rear-wheel drive whip manufactured between 1957–1979 in North America.

While there are no licensed vehicles in GTA 6, cars are recognisable based on real-world counterparts, with small visual changes to make them legally distinct. But the accuracy doesn’t stop at the car model — it also extends to how they drive.

That variety in handling is in part because Rockstar hired Lewis Bentley, a former Gran Turismo World Series competitor, to work on the vehicle physics team. Bentley announced the news in a now-deleted YouTube video.

“We put the auto in the Grand Theft Auto,” he said from the driver’s seat of his Lotus Elise. Bentley is best known for qualifying for the final in the GT Sport World Tour event at the Nürburgring 24 Hours, in 2018.

“Everyone on the physics team’s amazing,” he said in the same video. He claimed to have worked on GTA 6 for around three years in total, and is listed in the game’s credits as a developer in the physics department.

Bentley isn’t the only gearhead who worked on the game, however. Rockstar North has its own in-house racing team , and they’re pretty good on the track — they won a team-based 24h Nürburgring event back in 2022.

You can see this attention to detail in the game, both in vehicle handling models on cars and on the tracks. For the first time in the series, GTA 6 features a closed asphalt circuit called Gellhorn International Raceway, which stitches together a bunch of iconic corners and racing lines from some of the most famous real-world tracks in existence, turning them into the ultimate speedway.

articles.title: It Turns Out Jason Might Have a History With Mandy in GTA 6 After All
articles.summary: Mandy is obsessed with Jason in GTA 6, but there's dialogue that suggests they hooked up at least once.
articles.body:
As soon as GTA 6 was in our hands, an early game character quickly became a fan favourite: Mandy.

It's not hard to see why. Mandy certainly knows how to make an entrance, as she tries in vain to entice Jason away from Lucia . But alas, it is not meant to be.

Fans then did a little digging and found out that Mandy is almost definitely hiding a dark secret ; she's probably killed people. That makes her advances towards Jason — like insisting they were supposed to be married — look dangerously delusional. Jason might have dodged a literal bullet.

However, there is some easy-to-miss dialogue in GTA 6 that suggests Mandy wasn't basing her infatuation with Jason on nothing. You can come across this dialogue as soon as you take control of Lucia and find a meditation spot . The meditation sequence will play some audio from the character's past, usually centred around their insecurities.

AAAAAAAAAH — 𐔌 . ⋮ ιvσɾყ ֹ ₊ ꒱ (@ivysmores) November 25, 2026

In one of Lucia's medititation sequences, she recounts a conversation with Jason that she must have had off-screen after they got back in touch.

"Yeah, okay, we hooked up once, but, you know, barely. And it was a long time ago," we can hear Jason say in Lucia's thoughts. "You don't need to worry about her, Lu. Have you seen you? I know how good I got it. I'm not gonna screw that up again."

Of course, Jason doesn't mention Mandy by name here, but the wording makes it pretty clear it's her. Jason mentions not letting Lucia go again, so it would be after their initial breakup. That means the conversation likely happened after she was released from prison, meaning Lucia was living in the same neighbourhood as Mandy — and was aware of how obsessed she was with Jason.

In fact, another easy-to-miss scene does show that Lucia knows about Mandy. At the end of Chapter 1, during the sequence when you're running away from Jason's house as Lucia, you can find Mandy giving a statement to the cops (and, of course, exaggerating how close she was with Jason).

This game really has everything lol — Never break kayfabe (@Quadripolar_B) November 25, 2026

If you come out of hiding, Lucia can finally confront Mandy, saying, "Stay the f**k away from Jason, you crazy b*tch."

Better yet, the encounter gives us another clue that Mandy is a killer, as she tells the police she "wanted to light [Jason's] house on fire so many times."

With all of this in mind, it's no wonder that Jason was eager to stay away from Mandy early on in GTA 6 — it doesn't seem that she understood he wasn't looking for anything long term with her. Luckily for him, it sounds like Lucia is ready to run to his defence.

Mandy went viral pretty much as soon as GTA 6 came out, with countless social media posts discussing the character's motivations. Mandy actress Lexie Shoaibi has spoken out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame , pointing out that people keep trying to impersonate her on social media. Shoaibi has also revealed she spent around 10 days on set playing Mandy, but she also did a few other NPC voices while working with Rockstar.

articles.title: Losing Six Stars in GTA 6 Is Meant to Be Impossible, but Players Are Trying Everything From Interdimensional Portals to Hidden Bunkers
articles.summary: Losing six stars in GTA 6 is meant to be impossible, but players are trying everything from interdimensional portals to hidden bunkers to escape the cops.
articles.body:
GTA 6 's new police system is one of the most interesting things about the game. Instead of omnipresent cops, the police have have various levels of awareness, and you can use guile and cunning to outsmart them and escape.

There are still wanted stars, which represent how much of the police force is dedicated to hunting you down, but a well-considered escape plan can get you out of most kinds of trouble. Just escape the search zone, lose line of sight, and change how you look to get away.

That is unless you cause too much carnage. If you go off the deep end and cause real mayhem, you’ll eventually reach six stars. Six stars in GTA 6 sees almost the entire map become a search zone, and the cops will never stop tracking you down, according to Rockstar. If you need a pointer, here's how to get a six-star wanted level in GTA 6 .

If you hide indoors, the army comes along with a tank. If you jump in a plane, jets are scrambled to shoot you down. If you try to escape by car, attack helicopters perform a strafing run to blow you off the road. Eventually, no matter how hard you try, you will succumb to the pressure. Six stars, it is thought, amounts to a death sentence.

But is that guaranteed? Since GTA 6 came out, players have been looking for creative ways of breaking the rule around the highest wanted level. Using clever tricks, some are exploring ways to escape a six-star police hunt and return to regular gameplay — which should technically only be possible two ways: you die or get busted.

How to lose six-star wanted level in GTA 6

One player used a series of secret bunkers that you can open up to get access to a GTA 6 tank . Here’s the clip:

⭐️ LE PREMIER JOUEUR AU MONDE A RÉUSSIR À SEMER LES 6 ETOILES SUR GTA 6 ! Il est allé dans un sous sol rempli de bunkers pour réussir à semer la police. — La Twitchance (@LaTwitchance) November 25, 2026

⭐️ LE PREMIER JOUEUR AU MONDE A RÉUSSIR À SEMER LES 6 ETOILES SUR GTA 6 ! Il est allé dans un sous sol rempli de bunkers pour réussir à semer la police.

Another player in the comments said they managed to replicate this by swimming. “Bro, I actually did it yesterday. I managed to escape the 6-star wanted level,” they said . “Just keep diving underwater, and when your oxygen is almost depleted, swim back to the surface. Keep repeating this until you find a jet ski. Then ride it beyond the 6-star search area, and boom! You're free.”

Some players think the underwater cave system in Emerald Springs could be another prime candidate, since cops can’t send diving teams after you. If you head to Emerald Spring and look for signs for the Selkie Hole, there’s diving equipment you can use to explore an underground cave network.

Another player went to more extreme lengths to avoid the cops. After completing the majority of the long Vice City Easter egg in GTA 6 , they left the world through a portal back to the ‘80s. When they came back to present-day Leonida, the cops didn’t care about them or their Tommy Vercetti shirt anymore. Here’s that clip:

世界初？GTA6で手配度6から逃げきることに成功しました — ハイグレ玉夫 (@haiguretamao) November 24, 2026

“The cops in GTA are so overpowered that you can't escape them unless you go to another world,” said one commenter . “Now THAT'S how you escape the six star wanted level. That’s gangsta,” said another .

One fan also claimed to have escaped six stars by swimming into an underwater research station. Unfortunately, the video doesn’t actually show the six stars vanishing, but I guess they technically escaped, as long as they stay there forever.

articles.title: BioWare Fans Hit Out at EA for Selling New Dragon Age Merch After Killing the Studio
articles.summary: A new Dragon Age hoodie is available on the BioWare Gear store, as EA continues to sell merch based on BioWare's now dead franchises.
articles.body:
EA's decision to shut down BioWare sparked a mix of shock and sadness across the internet , with both fans and developers fondly remembering the many role-playing games the Canadian studio put out over the years.

The Mass Effect community has been especially vocal , given that Mass Effect 5 was cancelled alongside the studio closure . But Dragon Age fans certainly aren't happy either, and they're making it known.

Despite BioWare's closure, the BioWare Gear merch store is still being updated. A bunch of new items were added for N7 Day , but we just got a new Dragon Age merch drop too.

For example, the Dragon Age Inquisition Seven of Swords Nightmare Hoodie features a piece of tarot card art that appears in Dragon Age: Inquisition. Better still, the art depicts fan-favourite character Duncan from Dragon Age: Origins. But given that we're only getting this hoodie after everyone who worked on the Dragon Age series lost their job, it isn't sitting well with fans.

"Do not give #EA the privilege of royalties on IP they have killed, and will not sell or forfeit," one fan said . "If you want your voice heard and want to #SaveDragonAge and #SaveMassEffect, EA needs to reckon with the consequences of their bad financial decisions. #BoycottEA and licensed merch."

"Save Mass Effect. Save Dragon Age. Dragon Age was failed massively by EA. You destroyed what Veilguard could have/should have been because you pushed for it to be live service then backtracked. You never gave Dragon Age the chance it deserved," another person replied to the BioWare Gear Store's post promoting the hoodie .

"No studio, No Game = No money," Olarcadia said on X / Twitter . "What you're doing is a pure lack of respect." "It's so cute how you think putting out merch is going to make us hate you any less," onedcdame agreed. "Keep it. BioWare is closed, we're not giving you any of our money EA," replied SignWithBlood. "You should offer to sell back the IP to the founders, including the BioWare brand and name," added @inkpot__gods. "We bought merch to support the devs who made the games we loved; you fired all the devs and stopped making those games, so there’s no one left for us to financially support," said LouEaglesham.

It appears that the community plans to boycott EA's continued use of BioWare's IPs, at least until it allows a team of devs to make a new game in these universes. Right now, both Dragon Age and Mass Effect are on ice.

Dragon Age fans in particular have a lot to be upset about. The last game in the series, Dragon Age: The Veilguard, largely failed to impress the community. But it has long been known that the game languished in development hell and suffered from various changes in direction.

Former BioWare executive producer Mark Darrah recently shared the original vision for the fourth Dragon Age game , before EA allegedly mandated that it had to be a live service. EA would then go on to allow the game to be retooled as a single-player RPG, but The Veilguard had to be built from the bones of this live service work, meaning the developers didn't have time to return to this original outline.

It remains to be seen what EA does next with the Dragon Age series. EA is not in the habit of selling off IP, but if enough fans are boycotting the merch, it leaves EA without much to do other than just sit on it.

Rhiannon (she/her) is a freelance journalist who has been in the industry since 2019. She won MCV's Women in Games award in 2025 and adores RPGs. You can follow her on Bluesky at @rhithewitch.

articles.title: Isle of Man flexi ferry fares frozen but all others rise 4.1%
articles.summary: The inflationary rise is in line with the Steam Packet's agreement with the Isle of Man government.
articles.body:
Prices for Isle of Man ferry travel will rise by 4.1% from January with the exception of flexi fares, which will remain frozen at 2026 rates.

The Isle of Man Steam Packet Company has announced the inflation-matching increase, which is in line with the firm's Sea Services Agreement with the government.

Sailings can now be booked up to May 2028, and a new booking system showing the lowest fares across a month was launched on Wednesday.

Managing director Brian Thomson said the new system made it easier for passengers to find and compare the lowest available fares.

The Steam Packet operates daily sailings between Douglas and Heysham, in Lancashire, seasonal fast craft crossings to Liverpool, and weekly trips to Larne in Northern Ireland.

The Sea Services Agreement is a deal between the Steam Packet and the government, which owns it, that sets the rules for the island's ferry services.

The agreement allows the company to raise its fares each year by up to the August rate of inflation, as measured by the Manx Consumer Price Index. That stood at 4.1% this year.

The company's business plan for 2026 had projected a 3.3% rise in its underlying fares for this year.

Flexi fares, which are being frozen, allow passengers to switch to a different sailing without being charged additional administration or amendment fees.

Mr Thomson said the freeze meant "many families can continue to access affordable travel options without any additional cost".

Those booked early would also continue to "secure lower fares".

The fare announcement follows the launch of a new booking system, which the company described as the biggest change it had made to the way customers secured travel.

Thomson said the changes were "part of our longer-term approach to modernising our digital services".

articles.title: On Top of Everything Else, GTA 6 Is a Solid Stealth Sandbox
articles.summary: I came to GTA 6 for its wild car chases and explosive shootouts, but its the really solid stealth that has me hooked.
articles.body:
This is an opinion piece from writer Samuel Horti. IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games.

Grand Theft Auto is a boisterous, brash series full of loud characters and louder explosions. GTA 6 continues that tradition for many of its main story beats, chaining showy set-pieces into lethal car chases, but in my 35 hours roaming Leonida I've found plenty of chances to engage with its surprisingly robust stealth system. In some cases, it even feels like Rockstar specifically designed areas with sneaking and silencers in mind.

Illegal operations are lucrative robbery opportunities dotted around the map that hide cash, jewellery, drugs, and unique items – cars, weapons, watches – guarded by armies of enemies. I struggled with them early on: shooting my way to the valuables attracted GTA 6's menacing police, curtailing my heists before I could grab all the loot and forcing me to flee across entire counties while a chopper buzzed overhead.

Now, I treat these scenarios like stealth vignettes, my goal to remain hidden for as long as possible. I've screwed silencers onto my weapons and prioritized headshot precision over spraying power, carrying a pistol alongside either a tactical rifle or a sniper. My shotgun is purely for backup, just in case.

Skirting around these hideouts reveals hidden entrances. For Janjak's Garage in Vice City, for example, you can mantle a dumpster in a neighbouring alley to reach the garage's sheet metal roof. Out West, on the edge of Port Gellhorn, you can avoid the main gates of the giant Brooks Boatworks and slip through holes in the fence.

Stealth detection is intuitive. Crouching reduces noise, sightlines feel realistic, and you'll be warned by a yellow arrow over an enemy's head before they fully spot you, allowing you a window to nip back into cover. Knives silently slice enemies' open or you can choke them quietly from behind. And if you need space, you can whistle from cover to draw foes over, or throw bottles to distract them. It's classic stealth game fare.

But I've found that guns with silencers are actually the best option because they avoid the risk of an enemy spinning around at the wrong moment and catching you, knife raised. They mask shots almost completely: I've stood close to enemies and shot at others without being detected. Not everything in GTA 6 adopts Rockstar's general pursuit of realism.

Clusters of enemies are tricky because as soon as you shoot one, the others will spin and look for you. Here, I use focus mode to slow time and pop a series of headshots, plink, plink, plink. Three bodies thud simultaneously. I feel like prime Sam Fisher.

High ground is vital and from the right vantage I can survey the area, plan my route, and pick off enemies from distance. I always clamber to the loftiest point and use the D-pad to tag visible hostiles, which tracks them through walls. In a pinch, focus mode will highlight enemies through walls too, although only if they're nearby.

Some of the level design feels like it's steering you down this silent route. Back at the Boatworks, the first thing I saw after sneaking in was a platform lift to the roof of the main warehouse, high above every enemy. A drop in the ceiling led me to an empty top floor – I've seen this trick repeated in other hideouts, so I always look for ladders or other ways to reach the roof.

In the bigger compounds, staying silent for longer than a few minutes is a real challenge. No matter how many times I ran the Boatworks (I saved before I tried, and reloaded when I failed) I was always eventually spotted by some unaccounted-for enemy. But I reached a point where I could reliably clear the main warehouse floor-by-floor and empty the safe without anyone spotting me. That gave me a headstart on the police when I was eventually found, and by the time officers arrived I'd slipped back out through the fence, goodies jingling in my stash bag.

This feels like the first time stealth has been a core part of a GTA game. During standard stick-ups of stores and jewellers you can find back entrances, kill the alarm and erase security tapes – but you'll always need to confront staff if you want to grab absolutely everything. For that reason, illegal operations feel like the real test of your sneakiness, and I'm relishing each new one that pops up on my map. They have the feel of Far Cry's outposts: flexible, self-contained diversions that I can tick off whenever I need more cash, or just fancy a change of pace.

I've loved all my time with GTA 6 so far, but the best I've felt is when, this morning, I robbed Sound4Sound Studio in north Vice City. After hopping the fence I systematically cleared the parking lot and slipped inside, carving through the building, headshot after headshot. Nobody saw me coming, the police never arrived, and afterwards I could explore unchallenged, helping myself to every last bundle of cash. I drove off in a unique custom car, orange paint glistening, tens of thousands of dollars to the good.

I'd take a whole game of these scenarios. Thankfully, I've still got 30 left.

One final bonus of stealth: silencers are comically long, so now Lucia walks around Vice City carrying a gun taller than she is.

Samuel is a freelance reporter and editor specializing in longform journalism and hardware reviews. You can read his work at his website .

articles.title: I Tried to Get Six Stars in GTA 6 With Just One Bullet and Broke the Game
articles.summary: We tried to get six stars in GTA 6 by firing just one bullet and broke the game.
articles.body:
If reaching a six-star wanted level in Grand Theft Auto 6 is your goal, there are many different methods available to you. Raiding the military base for a tank is one way. Committing a horrifying beach massacre is another. But can you get there by firing just a single bullet? We at IGN had a theory that this was absolutely possible, and so spent hours in a fast food joint to find out.

When we say “by firing a single bullet,” we mean that technically speaking. Our theory is that your chosen character only needs to pull the trigger once. That’s because, when roaming around GTA 6’s open world and causing whatever brand of chaos you’ve chosen to, your partner will automatically take up the fight against aggressors, and is both invulnerable and stocked with unlimited ammunition. That means if you decide to walk into a heavily populated area as a couple and fire just one bullet into the crowd, your better half can commit the lion's share of the atrocities themselves, provided you just stay alive.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

We tested this out for ourselves, leading Jason and Lucia to the Taco Bomb in Gellhorn as our chosen arena of violence. Taking control of Jason, one bullet was fired into a poor staff member taking a break outside. Bits of brain now covered the forecourt, which somehow still looked like a more appetising alternative to whatever the questionable-looking beef was they were offering inside. Creeping cannibalistic thoughts pushed to one side, we walked back inside knowing our work was done. This public execution, perhaps rightfully, attracted a police patrol car to the restaurant, of which Lucia did not take kindly to their arrival.

Her love for Jason knows no bounds, up to and including unloading full machine gun magazines into any cops who want to arrest him. And who were we to stand in her way? Letting her take control of the situation was then required, honorably moving Jason behind the indestructible cover of an industrial refrigerator. Sporting an armoured vest just in case any stray bullets or shrapnel found their way around the corner, it was then time to hunker down in the kitchen beside that thick metal fridge, out of view of law enforcement. Crucially, this fast food establishment’s kitchen does not have a door leading outside, meaning the threat of flanking cops was neutralised. Luckily, they didn’t seem to spot the drive-thru window, which would’ve handed them a clean shot.

And there we sat for a good 45 minutes as Lucia angrily gunned down anyone brave enough to step into the restaurant. No more food would be served today, only death. The red of discarded hot sauce packets replaced by the blood of the fallen. The crunch of hard shell tacos drowned out by the crack of broken bones. All in the name of science. Could a six-star wanted level be achieved by us, the player, firing just one bullet?

Well, not this time. We could’ve sat here forever, bravely hiding behind a fridge while our partner slaughtered hundreds. Lucia was invincible, rounds of ammunition sinking into her skin to no effect. She had no shortage of ammo herself; with an unlimited pool of lead to reload from, she could’ve done this all day, and all for us. If that isn’t true romance, I don’t know what is. Day turned to night, and the restaurant workers diligently remained kneeling behind the counter and cowering for the whole sordid ordeal.

The problem is, our aggressors just… stopped. After a period of quiet, we chose to break cover and wander outside, only to be met by several non-aggravated members of law enforcement staring blankly at us. We had seemingly confused them with our methods of madness.

Because we’re so dedicated to the cause here at IGN, we tried all over again. Putting this first attempt down as an unfortunate glitch, we reloaded a save, made our way to Taco Bomb, and fired a single gunshot into our chosen test subject. And so, another hour of hiding behind a fridge commenced while our incredibly committed girlfriend peppered anyone who dared approach us with bullets. Armoured trucks eventually surrounded the exits, and the sound of helicopter blades could be heard above. But the same thing happened again. We even waited long enough for the rest mode settings on our PS5 to almost put the console to sleep.

It seems GTA 6 gets very confused if you decide to start a chain reaction like this, only to go passive for the next 60 minutes. Again, five stars were secured on the wanted level, but that sixth just wouldn’t arrive. The enemy AI’s brain could not comprehend what was happening, so we decided we simply had to intervene. If that sixth star was going to be ours, we’d need to get involved ourselves.

Thus, we thought we’d honor the place we’d called home for the past couple of hours, and end our occupancy of Taco Bomb with an explosion. A bunch of incapacitated, but not dead, cops lay writhing on the floor of the restaurant. Could just one grenade be our key to maxing out the wanted level? There was only one way of finding out. We ended the whole bloody affair with a bang, ripping the pin out of the explosive before hurling it into the mound of bodies. And that’s when it happened. Nirvana. The gates of heaven opened. Six-star paradise was ours to bask in.

So, what was the point of all of this? Well, more than anything, to confirm that you never have to worry about Jason or Lucia dying when roaming around GTA 6’s open world when not controlling them. Unlike in missions, where they can slip off this mortal coil, they can’t die in free-roam, and so you are clear to use them as superpowered distractions or unkillable meat shields if you wish. You don’t have to be as cowardly as we were, but if you have an hour free to watch an action movie scene play out while peeking out from behind the corner of a refrigerator, then that option is available to you.

There are certainly quicker ways to reach GTA 6’s highest wanted level of six stars, which means you’ll be hunted down until you’re dead, but this is one of the safest and requires minimal munitions from your own stockpile. Early on, we opted for the plane crash onto a beach, before mowing down all of the vacationers in a truck method, but since then, millions of players have been finding their own road to infamy.

But, in case you ever needed to know. Yes, it is possible to get six stars in GTA 6 with just a single bullet and grenade. As for just the single bullet itself… well, we’ll keep on trying.

What have been your wildest six-star stories? Let us know in the comments!

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .
